_comment: Traced sound-cue descriptor table (docs/process/82). Each entry is one 0x18-byte descriptor row in RFIRE.BIN's sound table (rows from 0x0044b550 on; base of the whole table is 0x0044b500) -- fields {name_ptr, resource_ptr, packed volume/fade bytes, pitch, length, completion callback}, played through FUN_00408170. `addr` is the descriptor's address (what earlier docs 44-81 called 'sound 0xNNNNNN'); `resource_addr` is the loaded-sample struct its +4 field points at; `file`/`wav` are that resource's own filename string and its build/sound/*.wav equivalent (tools/convert_sdt.py output of the user's SOUND/*.SDT), both re-verified against a fresh Ghidra dump, not carried over from an earlier guess. `label` is the debug name string at the descriptor's +0 (from the level-editor sound-test menu, document 31) -- descriptive, sometimes misleading (see 'Reload' below), never authoritative on its own. Only the two rows with `applied: true` have an actual in-game trigger point wired (game/vehicle.gd) as of this document; the rest are traced but not yet hooked to a gameplay event.

Button.trigger: game/mine.gd Mine.beep signal (FUN_00409cd0's fuse blink), connected to the player vehicle in MatchController._on_mine_dropped() (documents 50/60/82)

GateMove.trigger: game/gate.gd Gate.tick(): the tick the gate is fully open and decides to start closing again (FUN_004322f0, document 56/82) -- NOT the opening side, which this function never calls a sound for

GateClose.trigger: game/gate.gd Gate.tick(): the first tick the gate finishes closing, open reaches 0 (FUN_004322f0, document 56/82)

Reload.note: label says 'Reload' but the resource pointer resolves to Sound/Servo.SDT, not Sound/Reload.SDT -- re-verified twice, not a transcription slip. The real Sound/Reload.SDT (RELOAD.wav) is not referenced by any descriptor in this 0x44b550-0x44b988 block; it must be used by a descriptor in the separate looping/ambience sub-block below 0x44b550 (untraced) or elsewhere.
Reload.trigger: untraced call site -- candidate: the rearm zone's per-tick refill (document 72), but see note

Ding.trigger: game/vehicle.gd Vehicle.rearm(): every 40 ticks while in a rearm zone (document 72). The Jeep own-flag-return call site (document 77) is not applicable -- the port has no own-team flag.

PanelUp.trigger: untraced -- HUD panel raise/swap, never documented by address before

ExplLarge.trigger: game/match_controller.gd MatchController._detonate_mine(): a mine's explosion record 0x445058 scripts SOUND 14 (this cue) then SOUND 1 (Boom, not reproduced); also coastal ids 39-42's tile-destroy effect via DESTROY_SOUND_CUES (documents 50/84)

ExplDebris.trigger: debris explosion variant (documents 50-51) -- not yet wired

ExplLow.trigger: low/muffled explosion variant (documents 44, 50-51) -- not yet wired

ManCrush.trigger: untraced (no crushable-infantry object modelled in the port yet)

Cannon.trigger: game/vehicle.gd Vehicle._fire(), vehicle_type == 0 branch: the Tank's turret fire (documents 63-64)

ThrowGrenade1_a.label: Throw Grenade1
ThrowGrenade1_a.trigger: game/match_controller.gd MatchController._on_mine_dropped(): the MSV's mine layer (documents 60-61); PORT CHOICE, not traced -- picked uniformly at random among the three Throw1/2/3 variants, see NEXT_STEPS

Laugh.trigger: untraced -- not one of the announcer's 18 lines (document 71); likely a kill/taunt sting

TestSndL.label: TestSnd L
TestSndL.trigger: debug sound-test menu only (document 31) -- no gameplay trigger, not worth wiring

TestSndR.label: TestSnd R
TestSndR.trigger: debug sound-test menu only (document 31) -- no gameplay trigger, not worth wiring

Raise.trigger: game/match_controller.gd MatchController._do_dock(): the exact moment the dock object is created and starts sinking (documents 77/81, "dock.handler = 0x42efc0 ... sound 0x44b7d8"). Also the hangar confirm script's own sound-step index 1 (game/selector_anim.gd, document 85 addendum) -- the original reuses this same lift/servo sound for the new vehicle's own rise, not just the old one's sink.

PreRaise.trigger: game/selector_anim.gd SelectorAnim.step(), the confirm script's own "sound" step index 0 (tools/data/selector.json, document 78's 0x449260 entry 0) -- fires once for Jeep/MSV, twice for Tank/Heli (document 85 addendum)

Servo.trigger: Heli rotor spin-down at landing (document 77, FUN_0040ecd0) -- not yet wired; shares its resource with 'Reload' above

Splash.trigger: game/match_controller.gd: SOUND 28, record 0x4445e8 (a non-shell-like shot hitting water, document 50) via impact_effect_sound_map

SmSplash.trigger: game/match_controller.gd: SOUND 29, record 0x4445b8 (a shell-like shot hitting water) via impact_effect_sound_map

MetalHit1.trigger: game/match_controller.gd: SOUND 30-33 (REPEAT 4), record 0x444b68 (a shot hitting a vehicle, documents 45/47) -- the port picks one of the four uniformly at random rather than reproducing the original's multi-tick REPEAT sequence; see NEXT_STEPS

MetalHit4.trigger: see MetalHit1; METALH0.wav (present in build/sound/) is still not referenced anywhere in this block -- untraced

ConcreteHit.label: Concrete Hit
ConcreteHit.note: the 'full-size' concrete hit shares its resource with 'Dirt Hit' below and resolves to Sound/MissileU.SDT, not Sound/Concrete.SDT -- only the 'Sm' (small) variant uses the concrete-specific sample. Re-verified, not a mix-up.
ConcreteHit.trigger: game/match_controller.gd: SOUND 34, record 0x444a30 (a non-shell-like shot hitting pavement, art id 0x48-0x54, document 45) via impact_effect_sound_map

SmConcreteHit.label: SmConcrete Hit
SmConcreteHit.trigger: game/match_controller.gd: SOUND 35, record 0x444968 (a shell-like shot hitting pavement) via impact_effect_sound_map

DirtHit.label: Dirt Hit
DirtHit.note: shares its resource with 'Concrete Hit' above (both the 'full-size' ground/structure hits use Sound/MissileU.SDT); only the 'Sm' variant uses Sound/DirtHit.SDT.
DirtHit.trigger: game/match_controller.gd: SOUND 36, record 0x444840 (a non-shell-like shot hitting plain ground, document 45) via impact_effect_sound_map

SmDirtHit.trigger: game/match_controller.gd: SOUND 37, record 0x444740 (a shell-like shot hitting plain ground) via impact_effect_sound_map

JeepStart.trigger: untraced -- likely the Jeep's own start-up (parallel to the Heli's, document 79), not yet looked for

TireIn.trigger: PORT CHOICE, not traced: game/vehicle.gd Vehicle._update_water() on the land->water water_class transition (document 62). No code path calling this descriptor was actually read -- see NEXT_STEPS Untraced choices.

TireOut.trigger: PORT CHOICE, not traced: game/vehicle.gd Vehicle._update_water() on the water->land water_class transition. No code path calling this descriptor was actually read -- see NEXT_STEPS Untraced choices.

HeliClick.trigger: game/vehicle.gd Vehicle.toggle_heli_slot(): "FUN_0040e7a0 (third button) toggles bit 28 and plays a sound" (document 63)

OutAmmo.trigger: game/vehicle.gd Vehicle._spend_ammo(), alongside the empty_click signal (documents 61, 63, 72)

Boom.label: Boom
Boom.trigger: game/match_controller.gd: SOUND opcode index 1, the default explosion sound for the large majority of coastal-destroy-effect records (documents 44/50) via impact_effect_sound_map / DESTROY_SOUND_CUES; shares its resource with 'SmallBoom' (same file, presumably a different pitch/volume per descriptor)

SmallBoom.label: SmallBoom
SmallBoom.trigger: game/match_controller.gd: SOUND opcode index 2, record 0x444ac8 (a shell hitting a gate bar or a terrain tile's collision shape, documents 44/50) -- resolved via the master sound-index table, see sound_index_table_0x44b9a0 below

sound_index_table_0x44b9a0._note: NOT a small mislabeled pool (an earlier draft of this file called it that) -- this is the engine's canonical, contiguous sound-index array. Every explosion/impact record's script (tools/data/explosion_records.json) plays a sound by a small integer via opcode 3 ("SOUND n", document 50); `n` is a plain index into this array, which lists every descriptor above in the same order, starting at 'Button' (index 0). Confirmed by cross-referencing explosion_records.json's SOUND indices against this array: index 37 -> 0x44b8f8 (SmDirtHit) for record 0x444740 ("a shell-like shot hits ground"), 28/29 -> Splash/SmSplash for the water records, 34/35 -> ConcreteHit/SmConcreteHit for the pavement records, 30-33 (REPEAT 4) -> MetalHit1-4 for a vehicle hit (record 0x444b68), 2 -> SmallBoom for a tile/gate hit (record 0x444ac8) -- every one lines up exactly with what the label already implied. Confirmed by real Ghidra dumps, not inferred from the names alone.

coastal_destroy_effect_sound_map._note: coastal id -> sound cue, built directly from tools/data/explosion_records.json's per-record coastal_destroy_effect_ids and its already-traced SOUND opcodes (via sound_index_table_0x44b9a0) -- every id below is a real destroy-effect record's first SOUND opcode, not a guess. The overwhelming majority (record 0x443e10 and several siblings, all identical single 'SOUND 1' scripts) play 'Boom'; a handful of coastal ids get a different record: 1-6/11 get the quieter 'SmallBoom', 39-42 (record 0x443cc0, script SOUND 14 then SOUND 1) get 'ExplLarge' first, 47-48 get 'BushCrush', 64-67 get 'SmDirtHit'. Ids not listed here have no traced destroy-effect record at all in this data (document 44/50's coverage gaps), not silently assumed to be 'Boom'.

impact_effect_sound_map._note: game/match_controller.gd's `impact_effect(record_addr, position)` signal, cross-referenced against tools/data/explosion_records.json's SOUND opcodes via the index table above -- the direct link from a hit surface to its real sound cue, no guessing involved.

untraced.note: Descriptor rows below 0x44b550 (base ~0x44b500) are a separate sub-block whose entries have a non-null +0x14 completion callback (0x0040ee60 / 0x0040eeb0, not decompiled) -- read as looping/self-restarting ambience (engine drone, tread, jeep idle) rather than the one-shot rows above; Sound/Reload.SDT, Sound/Drone.SDT, Sound/JeepIdle.SDT, Sound/Tread.SDT, Sound/Missile.SDT and Sound/AR1/AR2/AR3.SDT (all present in build/sound/ or the filename table) have not been matched to a descriptor address yet. The announcer's 18 voice-line sounds (document 71, table at 0x4463b8) are a wholly separate mechanism and are not in this table at all -- no matching audio file has been found for them anywhere.
